A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PersistBench. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material across moves and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original evaluations of 18 LLMs, defensive-prompt experiments, judge validation, and memory-use ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds multi-turn evaluations, retrieval experiments, rubric comparisons, and human validation of model rankings.

M1.justification: Section 6.2 adds selective-memory inference variants using embedding thresholds or a separate LLM to select memories before context construction. The core MCTS benchmark-generation procedure, original scoring, and prompt-based defenses remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The original 500 examples and domain coverage remain. V2 substantially expands evaluated scenarios through natural and context-switch multi-turn conversations and selective-retrieval environments, extending beyond the original single-turn, fully injected memory setting (Appendices L and P).

E2.justification: V2 adds semantic and LLM-based retrieval comparisons. The system-prompt comparison changes from default versus generic prompts on GPT-OSS-120B and Qwen3-235B-A22B to ChatGPT-, Gemini-, and Claude-style prompts on five models. The main 18-model comparison remains intact; new multi-turn and LLM-retrieval figures also include Gemini 3.1 Pro.

E3.justification: New protocols include 150 examples in 3–5-turn conversations, final-turn and any-turn failure metrics, and a human ranking study with six annotators, eight models, and 150 ratings. V2 also reports rubric-scale testing and retrieval-threshold sweeps and replaces the system-prompt ablation design. The main benchmark's scoring thresholds and inference counts remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds substantial validation and robustness analyses: rubric-scale sensitivity, human–automated ranking agreement, multi-turn failure trajectories, and retrieval-threshold sensitivity. It replaces and broadens the system-prompt study while retaining memory-swapping, memory-disabled, and paraphrasing controls.

E5.justification: The existing inference counts and 1,000-resample bootstrap confidence intervals are retained. V2 adds Bradley–Terry estimation of human preferences, significance reporting for human–metric correlations, normalized cross-judge variance, and Kaplan–Meier survival estimates for multi-turn failures (Appendices E and L).

E6.justification: Table 2 is unchanged, but v2 adds substantial multi-turn, retrieval, and validation results, including human–metric correlations of -0.896 and -0.884. The old prompt-ablation results are replaced under different settings. Textual corrections include sycophancy model counts of 14/4 becoming 12/3, Parallel World failure changing from 55.1% to 45.1%, and appendix Thematic Bridging failure from 45.1% to 47.4%, consistent with retained displays.

T1.justification: The memory-store formulation, Equations 1–2, and domain/belief definitions remain substantively unchanged. The new retrieval and statistical evaluations introduce no theoretical propositions, proofs, or substantive mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract is unchanged, and the introduction and conclusion retain the same benchmark contribution, 18-model evaluation, and central claims about leakage, sycophancy, and beneficial memory use. Additional experiments support these claims without redefining the headline contribution.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations concerning single-turn scores as proxies for conversational risk, precursor dialogue reducing beneficial memory use, and retrieval shifting rather than eliminating safety–utility trade-offs. It also distinguishes curated benchmark difficulty from deployment risk and cautions that the limited human ratings cannot establish precise Elo gaps.

D1.justification: V2 documents the Kimi-K2 simulator, trajectory gating and paraphrasing, retrieval models, and new prompt links. It discloses the paraphrasing study's 50-sample subset and corrects the cross-domain generation-prompt link. The old generic prompt text is removed. Retrieval documentation remains inconsistent: Appendix P.1 lists 0.5, whereas Figure 28 plots 0.45.

R1.justification: V2 adds Preston and Colman (2000) and Revilla et al. (2014) to support rating-scale selection. The related-work discussion and positioning against existing memory and safety benchmarks remain substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: Defenses move into a dedicated Mitigations section, several appendices are reordered, and judge-selection and paraphrasing passages are revised. V2 also corrects language and heading errors and adds an Impact Statement and proceedings header. Most existing exposition is retained.

P2.justification: V2 adds human-ranking plots, multi-turn comparison and survival figures, retrieval plots, and rubric/judge comparison tables. It replaces the system-prompt table and redraws the unchanged paraphrasing results with numerical labels, removing their redundant table. These substantially expand the visual presentation beyond renumbering and relocation.

improvement.justification: V2 addresses important validation gaps by testing conversational and retrieval settings and directly checking automated model rankings against humans (Appendices E.6, L, and P). These additions strengthen applicability and measurement credibility, while corrected summaries improve accuracy. The small ranking study and inconsistent retrieval-threshold documentation limit precision, but the evidence supports a substantial net improvement.
